name: Pea Soup Green
lede: Pea Soup Green is a dull olive-yellow named for the color of split-pea soup, dated by Maerz and Paul to as early as 1430 but almost never photographed in museum paintings.

sections.title: An old food word
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates this name to 1430, on plate 10, swatch J2, making it one of the older food-based color names in ColorHub's library [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system, citing the same dictionary, classes it in block 105 [1]. A Wikipedia entry, citing the color-reference site Xona.com, lists the same hex under the same name; our library hedges that single web citation against the two older, dated dictionary sources [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[barf-green]], [[vomit-green]] and [[puke-green]], at 2.1, 
[[olive]] and [[mustard]] sit nearby in the same dull yellow-green family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a close match to Pea Soup Green in only 5, as photographed, essentially absent [2]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole: a saturated, fairly dark yellow-green like this is harder to mix as a stable paint than its food-color name suggests, and it is a modern color-naming word rather than a historical pigment [2]. The handful of matches are all from the 1800s and 1900s, led by Niels Larsen Stevns and Gustav Klimt [2].
